about: Round 3's declared gaps in D5's sanitizer records (t3/record.py; CLAUDE.md, D5): by host (L the laptop's Arch, W its Windows), the programs a record of a sanitizer need not cover, and why. Round 2's bench/coverage.json is round 2's and stays as it is. Every C++ target (the server with every external arm, v2's C interface, p2gen, e2e_requests) has no gap. v2's C interface, which the Go and Rust programs call, is covered by test_p2v2 under every sanitizer of its host.

mserver-go.reason: MemorySanitizer needs every library in the process instrumented; the Go runtime and the Go routers are compiled by the Go toolchain, which has no MemorySanitizer. Under ASan the Go code is built with go build -asan, and under TSan with go build -race, Go's own ThreadSanitizer, against an uninstrumented v2 library (the race runtime and clang's ThreadSanitizer runtime cannot share a process).

mserver-rs.reason: rustc's ThreadSanitizer and MemorySanitizer need the standard library rebuilt with them (-Zbuild-std and the rust-src component), which the lab's minimal Rust 1.99.0 toolchain does not have; without it their reports on the standard library's own synchronization are not to be trusted. Under ASan the crate is built with -Zsanitizer=address over the prebuilt standard library.

mserver-go.reason: Go has no AddressSanitizer on windows/amd64 (go build -asan is for Linux). Its sources are the Linux program's but for v2_windows.go, and the DLL it calls is covered by test_p2v2_dll under clang-cl's AddressSanitizer.

ct-msvc-tables.reason: H7's MSVC costs (t3/jobs/ctmsvc.py, bench/ct_msvc.py): the 22 compile-time tables are compiled one at a time and never executed; what is measured is the compiler's need (constant-evaluation budget, peak committed memory, object size), so the measurement is compile-only and no sanitizer record applies. Alex, 2026-11-03: "No record needed (Recommended)", as round 2's frozen text says.
